title: SYSK Selects: How Dissociative Identity Disorder Works
summary: SYSK Selects rerun, chosen by Josh, of the episode on dissociative identity disorder (formerly multiple personality disorder). The hosts cover the disorder's definition and symptoms, the related dissociative disorders (dissociative amnesia, dissociative fugue, depersonalization/derealization disorder), and its history from the late 1700s through early hypnosis-based treatment, the 1957 book The Three Faces of Eve, the 1973 book and 1976 film Sybil, the 1980s surge in diagnoses and the satanic ritual abuse panic, the 1990s lawsuits, and the renaming to dissociative identity disorder. They discuss Herschel Walker's disclosure of the condition and close with listener mail from Tony H. De Frieda seeking career advice.

segments.title: Selects intro and opening banter
segments.summary: Josh introduces this SYSK Selects pick on dissociative identity disorder, then the hosts banter about alters, forum posts, and the name change from multiple personality disorder.

segments.title: What DID is and how alters work
segments.summary: The hosts define the host personality and alters, explain trauma-linked coping mechanisms, note that alters may or may not be aware of each other, and describe how alters can differ in behavior, accent, and traits.

segments.title: Related dissociative disorders
segments.summary: The hosts distinguish four dissociative disorders: dissociative identity disorder, dissociative amnesia, dissociative fugue, and depersonalization disorder, and note common co-occurring symptoms such as substance abuse, depression, and memory disturbance.

segments.title: Early history: 1700s to hypnosis and Louis Vivet
segments.summary: The hosts trace early descriptions from the late eighteenth century, the first described case by Eugene Azam (spelled Ever Heart Gamelon in the transcript), the belief in a background consciousness, the link to childhood trauma, and the French patient Louis Vivet with several personalities, and Pierre Janet's account.

segments.title: Morton Prince and hypnosis-based treatment
segments.summary: The hosts describe Morton Prince's 1905 claim of curing a patient using hypnosis to draw out and integrate alters, and note that hypnosis was tied to the diagnosis from early on.

segments.title: The Three Faces of Eve
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the 1957 book The Three Faces of Eve by Thigpen and Cleckley about Chris Costner Sizemore, its popularity and film adaptation, and Sizemore's later book I'm Eve disputing the claimed cure.

segments.title: Sybil and the 1970s diagnosis surge
segments.summary: The hosts cover the 1973 book Sybil by Flora Rita Schreiber about Shirley Mason's treatment with Cornelia Wilbur, the 1976 film, Mason's paintings, and the jump in reported cases after the movie. They describe psychiatrists who questioned the case.

segments.title: Doubts, lawsuits, and renaming to DID
segments.summary: Herbert Spiegel's critique of the Sybil treatment, notes on suggestibility and hypnosis, the satanic ritual abuse panic and legal insanity defenses, 1990s lawsuits against therapists, and the decision to rename the disorder dissociative identity disorder.

segments.title: Is DID real and Herschel Walker
segments.summary: The hosts discuss whether DID is real, arguing sufferers are not faking, and describe Herschel Walker's book Breaking Free and his claim of many alters.

segments.title: Listener mail: career advice for Tony
segments.summary: Tony H. De Frieda, a recent returnee from teaching English in South Korea with an engineering degree, asks for career advice; the hosts suggest narrowing options and finding what he loves.

segments.title: Outro
segments.summary: Sign-off with show contact information and promotion.
